precepts.text: Thou shalt discontinue from thine heritage and serve thine enemies in a land thou knowest not: scattered from captivity to captivity under their religions and doctrines, we slumbered and would not recall who we are.
precepts.point: They that were ready went in to the marriage, deliverance from this wicked system, and the door was shut. To the five foolish he said, I know you not, the coldest thing you never want to hear from Christ. Watch, for ye know neither the day nor the hour.

note.label: THE FOOLISH, THE FAITHLESS

precepts.text: Thou shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee, and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not. That is the lawsuit the Lord took out against the nation: you serve your enemies, you forget who you are, and you walk around blind.
precepts.point: The beasts of the field, the fowls of heaven and the fishes of the sea are taken away with us. The repercussions run past the people and into the land itself.

precepts.text: He shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh. But blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord. That is the man who gets counsel, who reads the Bible and applies the commandments. The Lord set up men to guide us. But our people hate guidance. When they see you, it is low self-esteem: they see themselves in you, so they think, I am not anything, so I know he is not anything. That goes back to what was done to us in slavery.
precepts.point: As the partridge sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not; so he that getteth riches, and not by right, shall leave them in the midst of his days, and at his end shall be a fool.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
Jeremiah sets two men side by side. The man who leans on his own heart and on flesh “shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land and not inhabited.” He is dried up and alone, and he cannot even see good when it comes to him.

Then: “Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord”. That is the man who gets counsel, who reads the Bible and applies the commandments. The heart is deceitful above all things; your thoughts, your emotion and your intuition will destroy you. Nobody really cares what you think; it is about what the Bible is saying. So you have to be listening, in the word and studying, and not going and deciding for yourself without counsel.

The Lord set up men to guide us. But Black people hate guidance. When they see a man of the truth, it is low self-esteem: they see themselves in him, so they think, I am not nothing, so I know he ain't nothing. That goes way back, to what was done to us from slavery.

So the deceitful heart of verse 9 is the reason for the curse and the blessing here. The man who trusts himself ends in the salt land; the man who trusts the Lord and takes the counsel of the men he set up is the blessed one.

precepts.text: Cursed be the man that trusteth in man and maketh flesh his arm: a sister who says I trust him instead of seeing the test results is cursed in her trust.
precepts.point: An STD test is the example: six months of excuses about insurance and work is a red flag, and you wake up with the love bump because you were so worried about laying down with her. Refusing a test is hiding something; get multiple tests and go to the hospital with them, because people fake results with AI.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
“The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit.” The fool deceives himself and ignores the red flags. One of the plainest is trust in place of proof. Bishop Yawsaw told of a situation, and it is happening all over the nation: a sister was asked, Did y’all show each other your STD test results? She said, I trust him.

“Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm.” Miss me with the trust. I trust God. When you make flesh your arm, you make another human being your strength, the one you rely on and believe in. No: I need to see the test.

It is a red flag if someone does not want to go get tested. What do you have to hide? What are you scared of? If you have not been doing anything, you have nothing to hide; but if you are nasty, now you are scared and running from the truth. Six or seven months of excuses, I had to work, something happened with my insurance, and then you wake up with the love bump, because you were so worried about laying down with the sister that you did not care that she never took the test.

In this present world there need to be multiple tests, and you have to go to the hospital with them, because people are sending someone else in or having AI make them an STD chart, and you think it is official. That is the prudent man understanding his way. The sister who says I trust him has made flesh her arm, and the scripture says that trust is cursed.

precepts.text: She openeth her mouth with wisdom, and in her tongue is the law of kindness. That is a sister who stays green. If that verse is not fulfilled in your house, that is why the house is not blessed. And 'can I explain myself' after admitting every charge is of the devil; correction cuts both ways, healing the one corrected and the one correcting.
precepts.point: He shall be as a tree planted by the waters, that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when the heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green. Next to the water you never lack, and the sun does not burn you. Some brothers do not come to the war room for weeks because they do not want that water.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose hope the Lord is. For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river”. The one who trusts in the Lord and makes the Lord his hope, the Lord nourishes. A little plant next to a river never lacks water. When the heat comes the sun may be hot, but you will not feel it, because the hand of God covers you up. “but her leaf shall be green”: you stay green, you stay with wisdom.

Solomon shows what staying green looks like in a sister: “She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” That is a sister who stays in the green, the little plant by the water. When she opens her mouth, she opens it with wisdom, like someone who has understanding.

When that verse is not fulfilled in your house, that is why the house is not blessed. You wonder why you and your husband are going through things; that verse is not being fulfilled in that house.

The same goes for how we take correction. Asking to explain yourself after admitting to every charge is of the devil; Satan will make you look stupid, and it is better to just listen. The correction given is good for the one who gives it and the one who receives it. That knife cuts both ways: it cuts the one corrected, and the brother correcting says, I have to get my own thing together too. So do not be angry when a brother or sister checks you. Stay by the water and keep your leaf green.

precepts.text: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes, but the Lord weigheth the spirits. Everyone thinks they are righteous, but the Lord sees everything.
precepts.point: I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, to give every man according to his ways and the fruit of his doings. Most of us only see each other on the Sabbath on our best behaviour; six days a week nobody here knows what you are doing. The sister in Georgia bowed and said shalom for ten years while carrying on with the Uber Eats driver, and thought she was fooling the Most High.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

precepts.why:
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?” The heart is the mind, and nothing is more deceitful than the mind. Christ showed what comes out of it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

Yet Solomon says, “All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes”. Every one of us thinks we are righteous. Ask them: me? I ain't do nothing. Covetous spirit? Hatred? Oh, no. Judas would have said the same. All our ways are clean in our own eyes.

“but the Lord weigheth the spirits.” The Lord sees everything, and you cannot hide from the Most High. You can fool the deacon, you can fool the bishop and the leadership, but the Most High sees you, and you are not fooling yourself either. You know where you were last night, why you never called the brother back, and why you told her to hush before you answered the phone.

That is Jeremiah 17:10: “I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins”. Only God can search the mind, and he weighs what is really in it, not what we show each other. Read on: “Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established.”

precepts.text: He that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit. The verse names both the spiritual and the physical man, and that war between them will not end until Christ returns or you die in this.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

precepts.why:
“I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.” Most of us only see each other on the Sabbath, and when we come around each other we are on our best behaviour. Six days a week, Sunday to Friday, we do not know where you are or what you are doing. So what are you doing when you are not here? The sister in Georgia bowed, said shalom and happy Sabbath for ten years while carrying on with the Uber Eats driver. She thought she was fooling us, and surely thought she was fooling the Most High. You cannot fool the Most High.

Paul says the same: “And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit”. The one who searches the heart is searching the mind. And that verse tells you there are two: the spiritual and the physical man. There is a war, the spirit against the flesh, wicked against righteous, darkness against light.

That war will never be over until Christ comes back or you die in this. Some want it to be over and ask why there is so much evil in their head. Maybe because you are not reading enough. Brothers who do not know the scriptures will be the ones to betray you, because when they come to him he will fall. Ask yourself when the brother you talk to during the week last talked scripture with you. The Lord searching the heart gives every man according to his ways: not the deacon's way or the bishop's way, but yours. You are your own biggest enemy.

precepts.text: Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men, that I might leave my people, for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men; they bend their tongues like their bow for lies, they are not valiant for the truth, they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me.
precepts.point: Our enemies are the enemies of God, the other nations. Here we are unapologetically biblical; take it up with God.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee”. Even Jeremiah, who was not a wicked man, still went into captivity and had to deal with the same things as all the wicked Israelites. And look at how Jeremiah felt about his people, knowing how wicked we are.

“Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them!” Far away in the wilderness, just to get away from these people. They look just like him and he grew up with them, but he wants to get away from them. Why? “for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.”

“And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies”. Do black people do a lot of lying? Yes, we do. “but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth; for they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me, saith the Lord.” They move from evil to evil and they do not know God.

That is the black Christian. Do not let them fool you. They can quote the popular scriptures all day, John 3:16, neither Jew nor Greek, no weapon formed against me shall prosper, and say God got me. No, Satan got you. You and Satan are like my buddy and me. That is why the Lord says Israel shall discontinue from its heritage and serve its enemies in a land it knew not: a people who know him not.

precepts.text: He gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage. That is the heritage lost in Jeremiah 17. Rudolph Windsor notes that when Israelites lose their nationality they discontinue from their heritage, because the laws follow the identity.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Israel “shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”. We have lost our heritage and we serve our enemies, one of the curses. Who are our enemies? All the other nations, the enemies of God. Christians do not want to hear that, but here we are unapologetically biblical. Take it up with God.

What is the heritage we lost? “Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.” The law of life is the heritage we lost in Jeremiah 17. To take it, they had to break our bands asunder and separate us.

Rudolph R. Windsor, in From Babylon to Timbuktu, made mention that the Israelite culture is structured so that if you lose your nationality, you also discontinue from your heritage. We have a certain way of life as a certain people. When they strip you of your identity, what follows is your laws, statutes and commandments: you are not going to be performing the laws. Lose the identity and the heritage, the law of life, goes with it.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Ezra prayed, “O Lord, if thou suffer not thy servant, that we may pray before thee, and thou give us seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it”. Another word for culture is heritage: the same heritage Israel discontinued from in Jeremiah 17, the law of life.

The Psalmist shows it: “If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.” The right hand is your strength, what you work with. And Moses says, “from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” If you forget your identity, your way of life goes with it.

“If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth; if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy.” Forget the law and you cannot speak it; your tongue is stuck. Try to talk with your tongue cleaving to the roof of your mouth and you sound crazy. That is how Christians sound to those who know the Bible, with their doctrines; to other Christians they sound fine. We cannot prefer Jerusalem as our chief joy if we do not know we are the Israelites, so we become ordained ministers from the white man's theology schools and seminaries, and we sound like idiots.

So culture to our understanding is what we need back: the identity and the laws that go with it, so that fruit may come of it.

note.label: Exodus 20: The Ten Commandments

precepts.why:
The word says “Remember the sabbath day” because Israel would forget it. Jeremiah tells how: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

Israel was made to serve its enemies in a land it did not know. In this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion.

precepts.text: Cursed be the man that trusteth in man and maketh flesh his arm, the opposite of Hezekiah's trust in the Most High.
precepts.point: He sets captains over the people and comforts them: be strong and courageous, for there be more with us than with him; with him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God to help us and fight our battles.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord.” That is the opposite of Hezekiah’s trust in the Most High.

Hezekiah set captains over the people and spake comfortably to them: “Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that is with him: for there be more with us than with him: With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is the Lord our God to help us, and to fight our battles.”

Sennacherib made flesh his arm; Hezekiah trusted the Lord. “And the people rested themselves upon the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.”

precepts.text: A man cut off from his heritage was discontinued from the inheritance the Most High gave him, which is why the name has to be found written in this book of records to have a part.
precepts.point: The chief of the Levites, Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua, gave thanks according to the commandment of David, ward over against ward. This is the book of the chronicles, our ancestors written down in the record.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

precepts.why:
The Levites and the priests “were recorded chief of the fathers”, and “The sons of Levi, the chief of the fathers, were written in the book of the chronicles”. This is the book of records, our ancestors written down.

Why does the name have to be found written in this book? Because of what Jeremiah said would happen to Judah: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

A man cut off from his heritage was discontinued from the inheritance the Most High gave him, made to serve his enemies in a land he did not know. To have a part in that heritage again, the name has to be found written in the record, as the chief of the Levites and their brethren were written, giving thanks according to the commandment of David the man of God, ward over against ward.

precepts.text: The Most High commanded to bear no burden on the Sabbath day nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem, the very burdens Nehemiah shut the gates against.
precepts.point: He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
The burdens Nehemiah saw brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath were the very thing the Most High had warned about through Jeremiah: “Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem; Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.”

No burden on the Sabbath day, and none brought in by the gates of Jerusalem. That is exactly what the men of Judah were doing with their sheaves and asses and wine, and what the men of Tyre were doing with their fish and ware, and these are the very burdens Nehemiah shut the gates against. “Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city?” Jeremiah's warning to the fathers had gone unheeded, and Nehemiah would not let it be repeated.

precepts.text: The curse on trusting in man is tied to Israel being cut off and separated from their history.
precepts.point: This is why today, nowadays, we are separated from our history, according to Jeremiah 17:5.

note.label: Psalm 83: The Naming of God's Enemies

precepts.why:
God's enemies “have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones. They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” This shows that God has enemies, and Psalm 83 is about to name them.

This is why today, nowadays, we are separated from our history. Jeremiah shows the curse behind it: “Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord.”

The curse on trusting in man is tied to Israel being cut off and separated from their history. When our heart departed from the Lord and we trusted in man, the enemies were able to take crafty counsel against us, the Israelites, and cut us off so that the name of Israel is no more in remembrance.

precepts.text: I the Lord search the heart, to give every man according to his ways and the fruit of his doings, so our doings must be the fruit of the spirit.
precepts.point: He asks that His work appear unto His servants and His glory unto their children, that the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us, and that He establish the work of our hands. The Lord will give us according to the fruit of our doings.

note.label: Psalm 90: Teach Us to Number Our Days

precepts.why:
